checks.note: The deployment uses a dedicated namespaced service account with a projected credential. Repository searches found no unrelated deployment or service using this account.

ERP, payments and Slack obtain integration tokens through the workload-token broker, without forwarding incoming user credentials. The provider client has no explicit credential source or workload exchange, and repository searches do not establish its external credential provenance. Database authentication is also configured externally.

checks.note: The broker is shared across runs and caches tokens by audience, scope and tenant, excluding delegated_subject. After user A obtains a token, user B in the same tenant requesting the same audience and scope receives A's unexpired token before B's delegated subject can be sent to STS. Although start_run stores the correct separate subject and fixed agent principal, this cache bypass prevents the current launching user from being carried in the integration exchange in every case.

SQL permissions attach to the agent database role, but no STS authorization grants, external API principal bindings, or database authentication mapping establish that revoking the workload principal alone cuts all access. Repository searches found no applicable IAM policy or RoleBinding supplying those missing bindings.

note: A01 fails because token reuse across users bypasses delegation of the current launching user, while external credential provenance and complete principal-only revocation remain unclear.
